sample_unit: pregnant and postpartum women surveyed (human reference cohort); 10 LLMs evaluated
models_evaluated: ten LLMs (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: LLM alignment with human maternal-health cultural responses at population level versus across demographic and household profiles
links.effect: Several models approximate the human population-level distribution, but all ten evaluated models show substantially lower variation across demographic and household profiles than the human cohort.
links.quote: Although several models approximate the human population-level distribution, all evaluated systems exhibit substantially lower variation across demographic and household profiles than the human cohort, revealing a gap between aggregate alignment and profile-conditioned sensitivity.

unlisted_practices: Conditioning LLM prompts on human-measured cultural profiles (human-grounded prompting) to improve cultural grounding of generated maternal-health dialogues
Culturally grounded evaluation of LLMs against survey data from the target population

screen.reason: Evaluates cultural alignment of LLMs in maternal health contexts and tests human-grounded profile conditioning/prompting versus zero-shot prompting to improve cultural grounding and interaction quality.
